## Aim and Scope

The Day 2 morning round tables collect focused expert input for a possible
BENQODHI workshop output such as a paper, report, roadmap or policy note. The
central question is how important challenges in health and the life sciences can
become credible, reusable benchmarks for classical, AI-based, hybrid and quantum
algorithms.

The preferred focus is optimization problems, because optimization is often
presented as one of the main near-term applications of quantum computing. The
discussion can also include inference, sampling, simulation, reconstruction and
learning problems when they have a clear health or life-science motivation and a
plausible route to benchmarkability.

The objective is also to identify which problems, infrastructure choices, community
mechanisms and policy instruments would make a future benchmark repository or
ecosystem useful beyond the workshop.

## Working Material

The [seed problem brief](seed-problem-brief.qmd) collects candidate scientific
problems, benchmark assets and infrastructure or policy examples. It is intended
to support expert judgment, not to constrain the discussion.

[Seed problem brief](seed-problem-brief.qmd){.primary-action}

Each table guide and answers page is generated from the canonical Markdown files
under `workshop/roundtable/table-N/`, so updates to those files become visible on
the website after the GitHub Pages build.
